title: Whole-of-society development plans often include stakeholders formally while leaving consultation quality, civic capacity, and marginalized-group visibility uneven
source_unit: OECD and United Nations Development Programme, Making Development Co-operation More Effective Progress Report 2026
geography: Global Partnership partner countries and development partners participating in the 2023-2026 monitoring round; civil-society, government, private-sector, subnational, parliamentary, and development-cooperation actors

observations.period: 2023-2026 monitoring round; stakeholder participation in national development planning

denominator.unit: partner-country governments with national development plans in the Global Partnership monitoring frame

broad_stakeholder_engagement.unit: percent of partner-country governments, on average, engaging private sector, civil society, subnational governments, parliaments, and development partners when preparing national development plans, approximately

follow_up_dialogue_rate.unit: percent of partner-country governments conducting dialogues on priorities and results in follow-up processes

follow_up_gap.value: stakeholders engaged during plan preparation were not consistently engaged in subsequent priority and results dialogues

participatory_process_rate.unit: percent of partner-country governments engaging private sector, subnational governments, development partners, and civil-society organisations through a participatory process rather than consultation alone, approximately

observations.method: OECD-UNDP synthesis of the Global Partnership 2023-2026 monitoring exercise, including country reporting on planning, follow-up dialogues, and forms of stakeholder engagement.
observations.uncertainty: Country-level monitoring percentages do not show the intensity, representativeness, policy influence, or durability of any individual consultation; formal participation is not evidence of shared decision power.
observations.subgroup: Partner-country governments, civil-society organisations, private firms, subnational governments, parliaments, trade unions, development partners, and communities affected by development plans.
observations.counterinterpretation: Consultation can still reveal information and create accountability even without co-decision authority; participatory methods may also be slower, more costly, or difficult in fragile settings.

observations.period: 2023-2026 monitoring round; civil-society consultation quality and enabling environment

denominator.unit: partner countries with civil-society organisation assessments in the monitoring exercise

poor_development_partner_consultation.unit: percent of partner countries where civil-society organisations indicate development-partner consultations were non-existent, occasional, or selective, approximately

poor_government_consultation.unit: percent of partner countries where civil-society organisations indicate government consultations were absent or occasional and of limited quality, more than

cso_input_influence.unit: percent of partner countries where civil-society organisations say their inputs occasionally or consistently informed national development-policy design, implementation, or monitoring, approximately

stakeholder_perception_gap.value: governments generally assess the civil-society enabling environment more positively than civil-society organisations and development partners

observations.method: OECD-UNDP comparison of assessments from partner-country governments, development partners, and civil-society organisations across dialogue, legal-regulatory environment, and development-cooperation partnership modules.
observations.uncertainty: The assessment is not a comprehensive civil-liberties index, does not measure every organization or excluded group, and perception divergence does not by itself identify which actor is correct or establish causality.
observations.subgroup: Civil-society organisations, government officials, development partners, advocacy groups, and populations whose representation depends on civic-space and consultation conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Differences in assessments can reflect distinct roles, information sets, or expectations rather than deliberate exclusion; some governments may have improved formal access while quality remains difficult to observe.

observations.period: 2023-2026 monitoring round; inclusion and representation of groups at risk of being left behind

denominator.unit: partner-country and development-partner prioritisation frame for vulnerable and marginalised groups

prioritised_groups.value: women and girls, youth and children, the poorest, and people with disabilities are commonly prioritised

underrepresented_groups.value: older people, internally displaced people, and LGBTIQ+ people receive more limited engagement

high_data_availability.unit: percent of partner countries reporting high or very high data availability for identifying and tracking vulnerable groups

missing_disaggregation.value: migration, ethnicity, and Indigenous status are among the dimensions most often unavailable in disaggregated data

observations.method: OECD-UNDP monitoring of group prioritisation, stakeholder engagement, and the data systems used to identify, define, and track people at risk of being left behind.
observations.uncertainty: Priority labels do not establish resource allocation, service reach, outcomes, or the lived experience of excluded groups; data availability is self-reported and varies by country and indicator.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls, children and youth, people in poverty, people with disabilities, older people, internally displaced people, LGBTIQ+ people, migrants, ethnic and Indigenous populations.
observations.counterinterpretation: A group may be supported through universal systems without being separately named; disaggregation can improve visibility but can also raise privacy, safety, and administrative-burden concerns.

observations.period: 2023-2026 monitoring round; civil-society funding, advocacy, and institutional capacity

denominator.unit: partner countries assessed for the quality and predictability of civil-society support

cso_partnership_moderate_or_extensive.unit: percent of partner countries where civil-society organisations assess development-cooperation partnerships as moderate or extensive

development_partner_assessment.unit: percent of partner countries where development partners assess civil-society partnerships as moderate or extensive

restricted_or_limited_funding.unit: percent of partner countries where civil-society organisations assess development-partner funding as restricted or limited, more than

systematic_advocacy_share.unit: percent of partner countries where civil-society organisations report that development partners actively promote an inclusive and independent civil society in government dialogue, approximately

observations.method: OECD-UNDP comparison of civil-society, government, and development-partner assessments of funding predictability, partnership quality, advocacy, coordination, and enabling conditions.
observations.uncertainty: These are country-level assessments rather than audited grant flows or organizational survival rates; they do not show whether funding produces policy change, service delivery, political representation, or durable civic power.
observations.subgroup: Local and international civil-society organisations, development partners, governments, community advocates, and populations relying on civic intermediaries for voice and services.
observations.counterinterpretation: Restricted funding can reflect accountability, safeguarding, or donor constraints rather than only political exclusion; flexible funding can also create oversight and legitimacy challenges.

Official OECD-UNDP report landing page, publication date, scope, and full report citation.

boundary: This record adds a development-governance route from formal stakeholder inclusion through consultation quality, civil-society capacity, representation, data visibility, and implementation feedback. It uses publication-level monitoring aggregates and stakeholder assessments, not individual respondent histories, causal political participation effects, proof of policy influence, or a comprehensive civil-liberties measure.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official OECD-UNDP report page and the whole-of-society chapter were reviewed; stakeholder-engagement, consultation-quality, civil-society enabling-environment, vulnerable-group, data-availability, funding, and advocacy claims were cross-checked.
